result.rationale: The diff verifiably adds Discourse.ajax calls in removeMember and addMembers (group.js) with only .then() success handlers, and the controller actions (admin-group.js.es6) call them without any rejection handling. On a 403/422/CSRF failure the member list won't reload and no error surfaces. This is a genuine, verifiable missing-error-handling defect in newly introduced code (server can return 422 per can_not_modify_automatic), so it qualifies as a real (if low-severity UX) bug rather than a hallucination.

judged_text: Neither removeMember nor addMembers attaches a rejection handler to the ajax promise, and the controller actions that invoke them (admin-group.js.es6 removeMember/addMembers) also swallow rejections. When the DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/<id>/members.json call fails (expired admin session returning 403, CSRF token mismatch, or a 422), the bootbox confirm closes, the member list never reloads, and no error is shown: the admin repeats the remove/add with zero feedback and no console-visible path to recovery in the UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/models/group.js`, both `removeMember` (DELETE) and `addMembers` (PUT) return `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` with no rejection handler, so on a failed request the member list reload never happens. In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `removeMember` action triggers `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` inside the bootbox callback without handling/returning the promise, and `addMembers` similarly calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without handling rejections. From the diff alone, a failed 403/422 will therefore result in no UI feedback path in these actions and no refresh of `members` because the `.then` won’t run.
